title: Geometry Part 2: Right Triangles, Trigonometry, Circles
lead: This is the final content lesson. It builds on Class 20 and covers the harder half of the geometry domain: right triangles, trigonometry and circles. These are the geometry topics that appear most often in the hard second module.

parts.title: Part 1 · Right triangles
parts.html:
Pythagorean theorem. In a right triangle with legs a and b and hypotenuse c, a² + b² = c². It is on the reference sheet. The hypotenuse is always the side opposite the right angle, and it is the longest side.

Common whole-number triples save time: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, and their multiples such as 6-8-10.

Special right triangles. Know the ratios, and check them on the reference sheet.

TriangleSides
45-45-90x, x, x√2
30-60-90x, x√3, 2x, where x is opposite the 30° angle

parts.title: Part 2 · Trigonometry
parts.html:
Trigonometry. SOH-CAH-TOA is the foundation.

RatioDefinition
sin θopposite / hypotenuse
cos θadjacent / hypotenuse
tan θopposite / adjacent

Key property: sin x° = cos (90 − x)°. Since sin 30° = 0.5, cos 60° is also 0.5. If a question says sin a° = cos b°, then a + b = 90.

parts.title: Part 3 · Circle equations
parts.html:
Circle equations. The standard form is (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r², where (h, k) is the center and r is the radius.

When the equation is not in that form, complete the square for both x and y (the method from Class 11). This is a common hard Module 2 question.

x2+6x+y2−4y=12 (x2+6x+9)+(y2−4y+4)=12+9+4
(x+3)2+(y−2)2=25
Center (−3,2), radius 5

parts.title: Part 4 · Arcs, sectors and radians
parts.html:
Arcs and sectors. An arc or sector is a fraction of the whole circle, set by its central angle.

Arc length =angle360×2πr
Sector area =angle360×πr2
Degrees to radians: multiply by π180

These two formulas are not on the reference sheet. The sheet gives only the full circumference (2πr) and area (πr²).

A circle has radius 6. What are the arc length and sector area for a central angle of 60°? Fraction of the circle: 60360=16
Arc length: 16×2π×6=2π
Sector area: 16×π×62=6π

parts.title: Part 5 · Circle theorems
parts.html:
Circle questions are hard to answer from the picture alone and manageable once you connect each angle to its arc.

  • A central angle (vertex at the center) has the same measure, in degrees, as the arc it cuts off.
  • An inscribed angle (vertex on the circle) is half the measure of the arc it cuts off.
An inscribed angle cuts off an arc of 130°. What is the measure of the angle? What is the central angle on the same arc? Inscribed angle: 130°÷2=65°
Central angle: 130°

Tip. When a circle figure shows an angle or an arc, write the measure of the arc on your sketch first. Many circle questions are one step once the arc is labelled.

Beyond the reference sheet, the SAT tests these four properties.

TheoremWhat it saysHow it is used
Tangent–radiusA tangent line is perpendicular (90°) to the radius at the point of tangency.It creates a right triangle, so the Pythagorean theorem applies.
Inscribed angleAn inscribed angle is half the central angle that intercepts the same arc.A 100° central angle gives a 50° inscribed angle on the same arc.
Tangents from one pointTwo tangent segments from the same external point are equal in length.Set the two lengths equal to find an unknown.
Diameter ruleA triangle inscribed in a circle with the diameter as one side is a right triangle.The right angle is opposite the diameter, which is the hypotenuse.
A tangent from point P touches a circle of radius 5 at T. P is 13 from the center O. How long is PT? The radius OT is perpendicular to PT → right triangle with hypotenuse OP
PT2=132−52=144 → PT=12

parts.title: Part 6 · Hard geometry questions
parts.html:
Hard geometry questions rarely use harder ideas. They are hard because they hide the one useful relationship, or set a trap for a reader who is moving fast. The diagram rules from Class 20 still apply: use only what is stated or marked.

When to redraw the figure. Redrawing saves time when the given figure is hard to read.

  • The figure is tilted or stretched, so sides and angles are misleading.
  • The labels are crowded or far from what they describe.
  • Several shapes overlap: a triangle inside a circle, or a composite figure.
  • You need a clean coordinate plane to track points.

Copy only what matters (tick marks, angle arcs, parallel arrows, right-angle squares), keep the letters in the same order as the question, and leave room for your working.

Solving faster

  • Find the one relationship that unlocks the question. It is usually an angle pair from parallel lines, a similarity ratio, a right triangle made by a tangent and a radius, or the inscribed-angle rule. Write one equation from it.
  • Label what you need, then stop. Extra labels mean extra steps and more chances for an arithmetic slip.
  • Use coordinates when the figure is on a grid. Slope, distance and midpoint are often quicker than angle reasoning.
  • Use the choices. If they are far apart, an estimate removes most of them. If they are close, solve only until one choice is left.

How the test tries to trick you

TrapDefence
The figure looks symmetric, or seems to have equal sides or a right angle.If it is not marked or stated, it is not a fact.
A key word is easy to skip: parallel, midpoint, bisects, tangent, diameter.Circle these words. Each one is a rule you are being handed.
Your solution is turning into a long chain of steps.You have probably missed a shortcut. Look again for similar triangles, a circle rule or a coordinate tool.
You find a value on the way (the radius, part of a length) and it is one of the choices.Reread the question. It may ask for the diameter, the whole length, the perimeter, or twice the value.
Side lengths are given as expressions, such as x + 2 and 2x − 1.Set up the geometry relationship first, then solve it as an algebra equation.
Example. Line PT is tangent to a circle with center O at point T. OP=10 and PT=8. What is the diameter of the circle? Key word: tangent → OT is perpendicular to PT → right triangle with hypotenuse OP
OT2=102−82=36 → OT=6
OT is the radius. Asked for the diameter: 2×6=12

The radius, 6, will be among the choices.

parts.title: Part 7 · The Desmos application
parts.html:
• Circle equations: type (x − 2)² + (y + 3)² = 16 directly, or the expanded form without rearranging. Desmos draws the circle. Click the highest, lowest, leftmost and rightmost points: the center is midway between them, and half the width is the radius.
  • Trigonometry: to evaluate something like cos 45°, check the angle mode first (the wrench icon). Use Degrees if the question uses degrees and Radians if it uses radians.

parts.title: Part 8 · More circle and trigonometry facts
parts.html:
A radius perpendicular to a chord cuts the chord in half (and a radius that cuts a chord in half is perpendicular to it). This makes a right triangle with the radius as hypotenuse.

A circle has radius 13. A chord of the circle has length 24. How far is the chord from the center? The perpendicular from the center cuts the chord in half → 12
Right triangle: distance2=132−122=25 → distance 5

A square inscribed in a circle. The diagonal of the square is a diameter of the circle. A square of side 10 has diagonal 10√2 (a 45-45-90 triangle), so the radius is 5√2.

Arc measure from arc length. Find what fraction of the circumference the arc is, then take that fraction of 360°.

A circle has radius 12. An arc of the circle has length 6π. What is the measure of the arc in degrees? Circumference: 2π×12=24π
Fraction: 6π24π=14
14×360°=90°

Build a triangle from a trig ratio. If sin B = 5/13 in a right triangle, draw one with opposite side 5 and hypotenuse 13. The third side is 12 (a 5-12-13 triangle), so cos B = 12/13 and tan B = 5/12. The real triangle may be larger, but its ratios are the same.

Similar triangles have the same trig values. If angle E in one triangle corresponds to angle B in a similar triangle, then sin E = sin B, and likewise for cosine and tangent. A question may give the side lengths of one triangle and ask for a ratio in the other.

Which side is the hypotenuse? When a right triangle is given only by its side lengths, the longest side is the hypotenuse and the right angle is opposite it. With sides 16, 30 and 34, the right angle is opposite the side of 34.
